entities.summary: Cleobulina or Eumetis (Εὔμητις) was an ancient Greek poet known for writing riddles, with three riddles attributed to her surviving to this day. Born in ancient Greece, her exact birth and death dates are unknown. She was part of the cultural landscape of the Classical era, influencing the literary tradition of her time. Her works were likely performed at symposia and other social gatherings, where they were received by influential figures such as Aristotle. The riddles attributed to Cleobulina have been subject to various interpretations and analyses, with some scholars seeing them as a form of feminist critique of patriarchal society. Cleobulina's significance extends beyond her literary contributions, as she represents a key figure in the transmission of cultural knowledge and values from ancient Greece to the modern era. Her legacy can be seen in the many adaptations and reinterpretations of her riddles in Western literature and art. In the context of the ancient Greek cultural scene, Cleobulina's work reflects the social and political dynamics of the time, including the rise of the Sophists and the increasing importance of rhetoric in public life. Her riddles, with their clever wordplay and complex themes, continue to fascinate readers and scholars to this day, offering a unique window into the intellectual and artistic currents of ancient Greece.
